definition: A secured transaction is an arrangement in which a buyer or borrower (referred to as the debtor) guarantees payment of an obligation by granting a security interest in property to the seller or lender (referred to as the secured party). The property in which the security interest exists is called collateral. This transaction creates a legal right for the lender to take possession of and sell the collateral if the borrower defaults on the loan or fails to meet the agreed-upon terms. See secured transactions law.
